facade.notes: 1936 Standard Oil of Ohio station at night: a white streamlined box with a rounded corner, a full wall of glass showing the stock, the company name in the parapet band, pumps on islands in front with attendants serving; lit for night

why.note: 1930s oil companies branded with clean white 'modern' stations (the oblong box), easy to clean and recognisable
stations took corners: cars enter from both streets
